name: Samuel Tsao

I look for the simplest approach that solves the real problem, and expect each added system or abstraction to earn its maintenance cost. projects.title: Personal Portfolio
projects.problem_statement: A resume can list experience but has limited room to explain judgment. This portfolio gives recruiters a quick way to assess technical fit, then lets engineers and collaborators inspect the product problem, implementation, evidence, and tradeoffs behind each project. The challenge is making the deeper material easy to reach without turning the homepage into a long technical report.
projects.solution:
The homepage introduces my philosophy and interests. The comprehensive career overview leads with impact highlights and links to full experience and project stories. Visitors can also explore the same published experience through an agentic chat workflow, asking follow-up questions rather than searching every page themselves.

A Python/FastAPI service loads one JSON content file, validates it with Pydantic, filters unpublished entries, and calculates a content revision. Next.js fetches that content on the server and validates the response with Zod before rendering. The resume, career and project directories, detail routes, chat context, metadata, and sitemap derive from the same published entry collection. Production uses Vercel's internal service binding; the backend has no public API ingress.

The visual system uses restrained typography, readable prose, semantic headings, and clear links. The homepage stays curated while project and career directories expose every published entry. Detail pages include the problem, workflow, contribution, evidence, and relevant tradeoffs.

The recruiter-facing chat is part of this portfolio. The server loads the same published profile and project entries used to render the site, then sends that context with the conversation to the model. The browser sends conversation messages rather than a second copy of the portfolio. Chat history is not persisted; answers are grounded in published content and should say when the profile does not contain enough detail.

impacts.one_line_summary: Made my career and project experience directly queryable through an agentic chat workflow, so visitors can explore fit through follow-up questions.
impacts.full_description:

projects.title: Financial Analytics & Asset Recommendation
projects.problem_statement: A useful allocation depends on when money is needed, what losses a person can tolerate, and whether a goal can actually be funded. Ranking assets by historical returns does not capture those constraints. This collaborative project explores personalized allocation as a goal-constrained decision problem, combining a product prototype with a separate research workflow.
projects.solution:
The application prototype collects goals, risk preferences, constraints, and existing holdings through a guided questionnaire, then presents allocations and simulated growth. The repository also includes portfolio profiles and an experimental public-official holdings browser. Its original web recommendation path uses a bounded ETF universe and weighted rules; the Transformer and reinforcement learning work lives in the research pipeline. The existence of both does not establish that the web app serves the research model.

The application guides a visitor through a five-step goals and risk questionnaire, then uses those answers to generate an allocation across a constrained universe of twelve ETFs.

The recommendation flow includes a FOMO-adjusted tilt, and the application offers a thirty-year growth simulator to explore how a suggested allocation may behave over time. This is a planning aid; projected growth is not a promise of investment performance.

A separate feature lets visitors explore public-official portfolios. The repository README also describes notebooks for market correlations, technical indicators, and options Greeks.

Historical market series and company identity features feed a temporal Transformer that learns asset representations. A downstream Transformer combines representations with user context and generates a Gaussian allocation policy. Sampled weights run through a simulator with cash flows and goal withdrawals, and policy-gradient updates use the resulting reward. Cached representations reduce repeated upstream computation. The current RL worker uses a single Gaussian policy head; older research notes also describe dual-head variants.

The project plan identifies my role as simulation and architecture lead, responsible for repository structure, simulation, historical backtesting, and the optimization loop. Data/ML and financial logic have other named team leads. My resume and LinkedIn describe additional work across Transformer modeling, reinforcement learning, and evaluation. The system overview describes the collaborative project rather than assigning every module to one person.

The same public repository also describes research notebooks for market correlations, technical indicators, and options Greeks. These notebooks are separate from both the goal-based web application and the Transformer/RL research pipeline.

impacts.full_description:
Built a separate full-stack financial planning application with a five-step goals and risk questionnaire, constrained ETF recommendations, and a 30-year growth simulator.

The evaluation design uses historical holdouts, goal fulfillment, drawdown, volatility, and comparisons with S&P 500 and 60/40 allocations. Block-bootstrap scenarios broaden the sampled market paths, while chronological checks retain actual event ordering. The research notes have evolved alongside the code, so architecture descriptions here follow the reviewed worker implementation when the two differ. No independently verified outperformance result or production investment recommendation claim is available.

projects.title: Fog-Density Object Detection Research
projects.problem_statement: Study how fog-density information and detector architecture affect visual object-detection accuracy and inference cost. The repository separates pretrained baseline evaluation from the fine-tuned FiLM experiment.
projects.solution:
The research documentation describes matched fine-tuning comparisons for YOLO11n, YOLO11m, and DETR, contrasting RGB-only controls with predicted fog-density conditioning. It documents nuScenes, Foggy Cityscapes, and matched clear/fog Cityscapes scenes. Scene-level splits and aligned training settings support fair comparisons.

A separate experiment uses a frozen fog-density estimator to condition detector features through feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM). Predicted density informs feature modulation; the estimator and conditioning overhead belong in end-to-end latency measurement.

Research notes describe dataset checks, setup/subset/full profiles, resumable checkpoints, and comparisons using detection metrics, density-estimation error, and inference latency. The plan treats positive, null, and negative outcomes as valid. Do not infer an accuracy gain unless the saved results establish it.

impacts.full_description:
Built reproducible baseline and fine-tuning comparisons for YOLO11n, YOLO11m, and DETR across RGB controls and predicted fog-density conditioning.

The baseline study and FiLM experiment are distinct from separate squint/gating experiments and broader literature reviews. The linked repository documents the first two; no result is claimed for the other research directions here.

projects.title: Personalized Speech Recognition Research
projects.problem_statement: The group proposal describes an accent tax caused by ASR systems that overfit to Standard American English and fail to map valid accented pronunciations into expected text. It proposes cost-efficient, privacy-preserving personalization without retraining a large base model or uploading personal voice data.
projects.solution:
Approach 1 proposes a lightweight encoder-decoder accent-normalization layer that uses a user-specific pronunciation profile while leaving the base model unchanged; low-confidence recognition can prompt clarification. Approach 2 proposes a larger parent model guiding a compact on-device child model through self-supervised teacher-student distillation. The proposal also considers parameter-efficient updates.

The design keeps a user-specific pronunciation profile on the device and uses it when recognition confidence is low, with a clarification prompt if needed. For teacher-student adaptation, the proposal considers soft probability-distribution matching when parent and child capacity is similar, and hard pseudo-labels when edge hardware requires a much smaller child model. Raw audio and gradient updates remain local in the proposed design.

A rapid-decay learning-rate schedule is proposed to adapt quickly during the first five to ten user utterances, then reduce the update rate to stabilize the personalized model. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning is proposed to limit the number of updated parameters.

impacts.one_line_summary: Co-authored research proposals addressing accent representation bias through personalized speech recognition.
impacts.full_description:
Co-authored a group proposal and literature review on accent representation bias and personalized automatic speech recognition.

A rapid-decay learning schedule is proposed to accelerate adaptation during the first five to ten utterances before stabilizing updates. The proposal discusses latency, noisy audio, model drift, catastrophic forgetting, and reconstruction artifacts. These are proposed methods, not completed implementation or measured results.

impacts.one_line_summary: Proposed local pronunciation adaptation and clarification for low-confidence speech, with on-device teacher-student learning as a second research direction.
impacts.full_description: Proposed a local pronunciation profile with an encoder-decoder accent normalization layer and low-confidence clarification flow.

projects.title: Wordrix — Vocabulary Learning
projects.problem_statement: Vocabulary practice can become a memorization exercise disconnected from how words relate. Wordrix explores an interactive alternative: use semantic similarity as a hint so a learner can reason about neighboring concepts while learning foreign words. The product joins a small language-modeling experiment with a web game.
projects.solution:
A learner receives semantic feedback rather than only a correct/incorrect signal. The model represents words in a reduced-dimensional context space and uses a neural similarity calculation to produce hints. The historical project summary describes an interactive game connecting foreign and English vocabulary; detailed current screen behavior and language coverage have not been verified.

The resume describes crawling roughly 10,000 Wikipedia pages and cleaning about 50,000 entries. Preparation included stop-word removal, minimum context filtering, and topic-focused sentences, including animals and fruits. Training-data variants and within-group similarity-score distributions were compared to inspect model behavior. The application work spans an AngularJS interface and Java backend.

impacts.one_line_summary: Enabled vocabulary learners to receive real-time semantic hints through a word-embedding and similarity engine.
impacts.full_description:
Built a context-based word embedding model and neural similarity engine for real-time semantic hints.

The interesting engineering work is the connection between data preparation, representation quality, and feedback a learner can interpret. A mathematically valid similarity score may still be a poor game hint if too many unrelated words score closely or a topic is underrepresented. That makes examining the score distribution part of the product design, not just an offline model task.

impacts.one_line_summary: Prepared 50,000 cleaned entries from approximately 10,000 Wikipedia pages and compared data variants to evaluate hint behavior.
impacts.full_description: Crawled approximately 10,000 Wikipedia pages and cleaned 50,000 entries, including stop-word removal and topic-focused filtering.

projects.title: Trajectory — Financial Planning
projects.problem_statement: Budgets usually explain where money went. Trajectory explores a different question: how today's spending, contributions, and goals change the time needed to reach financial independence. The product connects immediate cash-flow decisions with a longer retirement trajectory, while making room for manual inputs and optional connected account data.
projects.solution:
Users configure a financial profile, inspect projections, and adjust income, expenses, contributions, property assumptions, and goals. A CSV import path and optional Plaid account connections reduce repeated data entry. Shareable profiles and backup/import workflows support portability. More recent development focuses on retaining edits, focused editors, reserve goals, and making uncertain connected data visible before it replaces manual values.

The reviewed codebase separates pure calculation engines, application services, browser controllers, and thin Plaid HTTP handlers. The profile codec versions a compact representation for URL transport. Current work also adds local persistence and recovery controls. An architecture document proposes a broader canonical plan model and repository boundary; that target design is not described here as a completed migration.

Losing a plan or silently substituting a bad balance would undermine the product more than a missing chart. Development notes record fixes for startup hydration overwriting restored values, storage failures, cross-tab conflicts, incomplete provider pagination, and negative or unknown balances. The revised flows retain manual values when connected data needs review, preserve prior records during writes, and expose backup and recovery options.

impacts.one_line_summary: Connected retirement, loan, spending, and investment scenarios in one planning workflow with shareable profiles.

projects.title: MTG Vault — Collection Tracker
projects.problem_statement: Cataloging a physical card collection is repetitive work. A collector needs to distinguish sets, printings, finishes, condition, and language, often for thousands of cards. A complete database form is not necessarily a fast capture experience. MTG Vault starts with the entry loop, then adds browsing, valuation estimates, and portability around it.
projects.solution:
A collector types a card name, chooses a set and printing with the keyboard, selects finish and condition, and presses Enter. They can immediately begin the next card. Existing matching variants increase in quantity rather than becoming duplicate rows. Browsing adds search, sorting, details, and collection statistics, while mobile uses a dedicated navigation and selection layout.

Scryfall supplies card identity, images, printing metadata, and reference prices. A variant identity combines the card, set, style, finish, condition, and language. Storage interfaces support Google Sheets through CSV reads and Apps Script writes, plus a local CSV representation in browser storage. A sync queue merges matching operations and sends batches rather than a separate request for each keystroke.

CSV import detects common collection formats, normalizes aliases, resolves printings, and previews results with found, unfound, and error counts. Export targets include collector and marketplace workflows. For remote write failures, the documented recovery paths include an unsynced CSV backup and switching to local storage. Shared collection mode is read-only; it is a separate experience from editing an owned collection.

impacts.one_line_summary: Made card cataloging usable through keyboard-driven desktop entry and mobile workflows, including printing, finish, condition, and language selection.
impacts.full_description:
Built keyboard-driven card entry with set, printing, finish, condition, and language selection.

The repository includes tests for card identity, CSV parsing, import behavior, collection actions, sync queues, and Moxfield handling. The product document distinguishes intended behavior from remaining implementation gaps. Price fields are market references, not realizable sale prices, and remote storage depends on the user's sheet and Apps Script setup. No measured entry-speed advantage, large-scale multi-user guarantee, or commerce capability is claimed.

projects.title: Tsao Wang Family Foundation Website
projects.problem_statement: A nonprofit needs to keep resources and messages current without making every edit a developer task. The foundation website prioritizes a content workflow that nontechnical administrators can operate, along with clear resource navigation for English and Traditional Chinese readers.
projects.solution:
An administrator edits text, image links, and resource records in a Google Spreadsheet. The website reads the published sheet data when visitors load the page and maps it into reusable sections. Visitors browse foundation information and resource categories with language-specific content. This puts routine publishing into a familiar editing tool while keeping the public interface separate.

The reviewed project uses React and Vite, reusable page and section components, a custom CSS-variable design system, and PapaParse for published CSV data. Fetch functions load resources and messages, parse column headers, and convert rows into page content. Language-specific sheet data supplies translated content rather than automatically translating a single source.

impacts.one_line_summary: Led developer and UX collaboration on a nonprofit website designed for nontechnical administrators to use and maintain.
impacts.full_description:
Led collaboration with a developer and UX contributor to design the nonprofit website.

LinkedIn describes leading collaboration with a developer and a UX contributor. The local code and README support the component-based site and spreadsheet content architecture, while the changelog records work on responsive navigation, consistent page layout, branding, metadata, and dropdown behavior. These describe the team's implementation; they do not attribute every code change to me personally.
